title: Encapsulation

options.t: Inheriting behaviour from a base class
Bundling data with the methods that operate on it and restricting direct access to internal state
Having many forms of a method

answer: Hide internal state behind a controlled interface.
explanation: Encapsulation lets an object protect its invariants (e.g. a BankAccount balance can only change through Deposit/Withdraw that validate amounts).

title: Polymorphism

options.t: Defining two methods with the same name and different parameters
Calling a method through a base type reference and having the derived type's implementation execute

answer: Dynamic dispatch through a common base type or interface.
explanation: It lets code depend on abstractions (`IShape.Area()`) while behaviour varies by concrete type, which is the foundation of the Open/Closed principle.

title: Composition over inheritance
body: Why is composition often preferred over inheritance?

options.t: Inheritance is not supported in modern languages
It assembles behaviour from small, replaceable collaborators, avoiding fragile deep hierarchies and tight coupling to base-class internals

explanation: Inheritance models a stable 'is-a' relationship; composition ('has-a') lets behaviour change at runtime and supports dependency injection and testing with fakes.

title: Overloading vs overriding

options.t: Overriding is resolved at compile time
Overloading chooses among same-named methods by parameter list at compile time; overriding replaces a virtual method's implementation, resolved at runtime
Overloading changes the return type only

explanation: Overload resolution uses the static types of arguments; overriding uses the runtime type of the receiver.

title: Single Responsibility Principle
body: What does the Single Responsibility Principle state?

options.t: A class should have only one method
A module should have one reason to change — it should serve one actor/responsibility
Each project should have one class
Functions must be under ten lines

explanation: An `InvoiceService` that calculates totals, renders PDFs and sends emails changes for three different reasons; split it into collaborators.

title: Open/Closed Principle
body: Which design follows the Open/Closed Principle for adding new payment methods?

options.t: A switch statement in PaymentService that grows with every new method
An IPaymentProcessor interface with one implementation per method, selected at runtime, so new methods are added as new classes
Storing payment logic in the database

answer: Extend with new implementations instead of editing existing code.
explanation: Open for extension, closed for modification: polymorphism (strategy pattern) and DI registration let you add behaviour without touching tested code.

title: Liskov Substitution Principle
body: Which is a classic LSP violation?

options.t: A Dog class inheriting from Animal
A Square inheriting from Rectangle where setting Width also changes Height, breaking code that expects independent sides

answer: Square/Rectangle — the subtype breaks base-type expectations.
explanation: Subtypes must honour the base contract: no stronger preconditions, no weaker postconditions, no surprising exceptions (e.g. throwing NotSupportedException from an inherited method).

title: Interface Segregation Principle
body: What does the Interface Segregation Principle recommend?

options.t: Clients should not be forced to depend on methods they do not use; prefer small, role-specific interfaces

explanation: A `IMultiFunctionDevice` with Print/Scan/Fax forces a simple printer to stub methods; split into IPrinter, IScanner, IFax.

title: Dependency Inversion Principle
body: What does the Dependency Inversion Principle state?

options.t: Low-level modules should depend on high-level modules
High-level policy should depend on abstractions, and low-level details should implement those abstractions

explanation: DIP is the principle; dependency injection is a technique to supply implementations. In clean architecture the application layer defines interfaces (e.g. IEmailSender) that infrastructure implements.

title: Singleton pattern
body: Which pattern ensures a class has a single instance with a global access point?
explanation: In .NET prefer registering a service with a singleton lifetime in DI over a static Instance property: it stays testable and the lifetime is explicit. Singletons must be thread-safe.

title: Strategy pattern
body: Which pattern encapsulates interchangeable algorithms behind a common interface?
explanation: Example: IShippingCostStrategy with Standard/Express/Free implementations chosen at runtime. It removes conditional logic and supports the Open/Closed principle.

title: Observer pattern
body: In C#, which language feature directly implements the Observer pattern?
explanation: Subjects notify subscribers without knowing their concrete types. Unsubscribe to avoid memory leaks with long-lived publishers.

title: Decorator pattern
body: Which pattern adds behaviour to an object by wrapping it with another object implementing the same interface?
explanation: Examples: `BufferedStream` wrapping `FileStream`, a `CachingRepository` wrapping a repository, or HttpClient DelegatingHandlers for logging/retries. Decorators compose without subclass explosion.

title: Factory Method
body: What problem does the Factory Method pattern address?

options.t: Letting subclasses or a dedicated method decide which concrete class to instantiate, so callers depend only on an abstraction

explanation: Callers ask for an `INotificationSender` and the factory returns Email/SMS/Push implementations based on configuration. Abstract Factory creates families of related objects.

title: Unit of Work in EF Core
body: In Entity Framework Core, which type already implements the Unit of Work pattern?

options.e: DbSet is closer to a repository.

explanation: DbContext tracks changes across entities and commits them in one SaveChanges call (one transaction). Wrapping EF in generic repositories often adds little; use specific query services or the DbContext directly behind an application interface.

title: Clean Architecture dependency rule
body: What is the dependency rule in Clean Architecture?

options.t: Outer layers must not depend on inner layers
Source-code dependencies point inward: the domain and application layers know nothing about frameworks, UI or databases
Every layer depends on every other layer

explanation: Infrastructure implements interfaces defined by the application layer, keeping business rules testable and independent of EF Core, ASP.NET Core or external services.
